title: Page through warehouse codes the same way on every instance

blocks.text: Operations staff page through the company's warehouse codes in the admin console, a few codes per page, in alphabetical order. They report that a page sometimes lists codes in no recognisable order, that the same page number shows different codes from one visit to the next, and that some warehouses never appear on any page.

The console runs on several instances behind a load balancer, and each one gets the codes from the inventory service as a `Set` that promises no order. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/WarehouseDirectory.java`: `page(page, size)` returns page `page` (counted from 0) of `size` codes in alphabetical order, so that paging from the first page to the last shows every code exactly once, whichever instance serves each page.

cases.says: codes that already arrive in alphabetical order give the first page, and a page past the end is empty
the first page is the alphabetically first codes, whatever order the set hands them out in
a later page holds the codes that come next alphabetically, not the next ones the set hands out, sorted
going through every page shows every code once, the last page partly filled

origin.section: limit and skip Count in Encounter Order, and HashSet and Set.of Have None

concepts: limit and skip take the first elements in the stream's encounter order, so paging an unordered source gives different pages from run to run unless it is sorted first, before the skip.
